Closed-loop systems

Source: R/lqr.R
ctrl_closed_loop.Rd

Build the closed loop of a plant with a controller.

Usage

ctrl_closed_loop(plant, controller, include_control = TRUE)

Arguments

plant

Plant model.

controller

A ctrl_lqr object, a gain matrix K, a ctrl_lqg object, or a ctrl_ss / ctrl_tf error-feedback controller.

include_control

Append the control signal to the outputs.

Value

A ctrl_ss model.

Details

  • With an LQR or other static state feedback (ctrl_lqr, or a matrix K), the control law is \(u = -K x + v\), where v is an external input. The closed loop is \(\dot x = (A - BK) x + B v\), \(y = (C - DK) x + D v\), with outputs y followed (when include_control = TRUE) by the control signal u.

  • With an LQG controller (see ctrl_lqg()) the controller is a dynamic system from the measurement to the input, connected in positive feedback u = K_c(y) (the controller already contains the minus sign), with an additive input disturbance v at the plant input. States are the plant states followed by the controller states.

  • With a dynamic ctrl_ss or ctrl_tf controller Cs acting on the error \(r - y\), the loop is the unity negative feedback \(y = (I + G C_s)^{-1} G C_s r\).

Examples

plant <- ctrl_ss(matrix(c(0, 1, -2, -3), 2, byrow = TRUE), c(0, 1), c(1, 0))
cl <- ctrl_closed_loop(plant, ctrl_lqr(plant, diag(2), 1))
ctrl_poles(cl)
#> [1] -1.000000+0i -2.236068+0i
